en: We've said her name half a dozen times today — under Sólheimajökull, off Dýrhólaey, at the church on the hill, in the cairn field, on Hjörleifshöfði. **Here's the volcano itself.** And the biggest threat on the South Coast doesn't look like a threat — it's a **white ice cap, peaceful and silent.**
ctx: opening hook line — tour 7.0 / Fellsfjara → Vík 2 hour drive folks / Katla

en: Iceland's world-famous parliament at Þingvellir? Not even the first. The original ran right here — set up by the founder's son. Nepotism: also a Viking value.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Borgarnes / ⚖️ Kjalarnes

en: In a moment you'll have **40 metres of North Atlantic directly over your head**. Your ears will notice before you do.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Borgarnes / 🕳️ Hvalfjörður Tunnel

en: How does a fjord get named "Whale fjord"? Officially: whales. In the folklore: **one specific whale** — with a red head, a grudge, and a body count.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Borgarnes / 🐋 Hvalfjörður

en: There is a **whale bone in that mountain, 85 metres above the sea**. Nobody carried it up there. The sea delivered.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Borgarnes / ⛰️ Akrafjall

en: Before 1981, the Ring Road took a **four-kilometre detour inland** to get across this water. Then we built **520 metres of bridge** and kept the change.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Borgarnes / 🌉 Borgarfjarðarbrú

en: Toilet stop, yes — but you are parked inside a **saga graveyard**. Nearly everyone in the first act of Egils saga is buried within sight of this forecourt.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Borgarnes / 🪦 Borgarnes

en: Why does this peninsula have volcanoes at all? The plate boundary **left six million years ago** — packed up, moved to Reykjanes — and Snæfellsnes **kept erupting anyway**. Most recently in the **10th century**. Some things don't take the hint.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Borgarnes → Selvallafoss / 🌋 Iceland's First Rift Zone

en: Everything on your right for the next while — one volcanic system. **Ninety kilometres** of it, from Kolgrafarfjörður all the way back to Borgarfjörður. And in **1148** it hosted the deadliest fire in Icelandic history — at a **dinner party**.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Borgarnes → Selvallafoss / 🔥 Hítardalur & Ljósufjöll

en: That ring on the left wasn't built by anyone. **200 metres long, 50 metres deep**, walls in places just a thin crust of lava — and the name says exactly what it looks like: **Eldborg**. Fire-fortress.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Borgarnes → Selvallafoss / 🌋 Eldborg

en: Who stacked all those pillars? Nobody. That wall on the right did it to itself — and the reason it's **hexagons** is the same reason bees build hexagons: **geometry only offers so many options**.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Borgarnes → Selvallafoss / 🪨 Gerðuberg

en: The road under you is exactly as old as **Wikipedia** — both launched in **2001** — and the flat-topped mountains beside it were built **under an ice sheet**. Brand-new tarmac, Ice Age scenery, no middle ground.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Borgarnes → Selvallafoss / ⛰️ Vatnaleið

en: Icelandic farmers named **everything**. Seventy-nine separate features on this one abandoned farm — every gully, every boulder, the rock where the hidden people sang. They did not name the waterfall. And the name on your map today? Somebody in tourism made it up.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Selvallafoss / 💧 Fossá

en: Water pours into this lake all day long. **Nothing flows out of it.** Not a stream, not a trickle, nothing above ground. Somewhere under that lava the whole lake is quietly draining away — and nobody has ever proved where it goes.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Selvallafoss / 🌀 Selvallavatn

en: Iceland's first recorded construction contract: clear a road through this lava and marry the farmer's daughter. **The contractors finished the job. They should have read the fine print.**
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Selvallafoss → Kirkjufell / 🪨 Berserkjahraun

en: Half this bus already has this mountain as a screensaver. My job isn't to introduce it — **it's to correct it.**
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Kirkjufell / ⛰️ Kirkjufell

en: How do you get rid of eighteen ghosts? Iceland's answer, year 1000: **take them to court.** Charges, pleadings, verdicts — and closing statements from the defendants.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Kirkjufell → Ólafsvík / 👻 Fróðá

en: How does a village lose everything? A river moves **once** — and a king in Copenhagen signs a licence for the neighbours.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Ólafsvík / ⚓ Ólafsvík

en: What's more dangerous than being the richest man in Iceland? **Standing between English merchants and their cod.** In 1467, right here, the King of Denmark's own governor found out.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Ólafsvík → Djúpalónssandur / 🪓 Björn the Rich

en: Anyone here fly in from further away than the edge of **Antarctica**? No? Then every one of us has been out-travelled by the small white birds nesting beside the car park.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Ólafsvík → Djúpalónssandur / 🐦 The Tern Capital

en: There's a painting of **Christopher Columbus** in the parish hall on that hill. The entire paper trail behind it runs through **a Danish short story serialised in a Winnipeg newspaper in 1889.**
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Ólafsvík → Djúpalónssandur / ⛪ Hellissandur, Ingjaldshóll & the Columbus Story

en: A crater staircase that won a **major international design prize**. Its own architects call it **"the stairway to heaven and hell."** It has 396 steps, and yes — somebody counted.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Ólafsvík → Djúpalónssandur / 🪜 Saxhóll

en: How did you apply for a job on this coast? Four stones on a beach: **154 kilos, 100, 54 — and 23, named "Useless."** Lift the third one, or row home.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Djúpalónssandur / 💪 Djúpalónssandur & Dritvík

en: When the farm at the lighthouse ran out of water, they didn't dig a new well. They walked to a **lava cave** and **scooped water out of the top of it for the cows.**
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Djúpalónssandur → Arnarstapi / 🕳️ Malarrif & Vatnshellir

en: Those two towers are **not** rocks the sea piled up. They're the **plumbing of a dead volcano** — and on the cliff beside them, a poet once beat the devil in a rhyming contest. We have the verses.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Djúpalónssandur → Arnarstapi / 🪨 Lóndrangar

en: The most famous thing ever written about this mountain was written by a Frenchman **who never came here**. The mountain has not commented.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Djúpalónssandur → Arnarstapi / 🌋 Snæfellsjökull

en: A woman born on that slope had a baby **on the far side of the Atlantic** — about **five centuries** before Columbus's crew ever laid eyes on it.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Djúpalónssandur → Arnarstapi / 🧭 Guðríður Þorbjarnardóttir

en: Time to meet the landlord of this whole coast. **Bárður Snæfellsás** — giants on his father's side, trolls in the family, raised by a creature living inside a mountain — and the first thing the saga has him do on arrival here is **take a bath**.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Djúpalónssandur → Arnarstapi / 🛁 Bárðarlaug

en: Basalt columns are supposed to stand up straight. Half of the ones on this coast are **lying flat on their sides** — and the rock is following the rules by doing it.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Arnarstapi / 🐦 The Arnarstapi Cliffs

en: Six metres of stacked stone, close to **300 tonnes** — a saga giant guarding the harbour. And the detail few guides know: it's also **a family's gravestone**.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Arnarstapi / 🗿 The Bárður Statue

en: This little cove was once the **seat of government for western Iceland**. Then somebody took the government building apart, put it on a boat, and **shipped it away**.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Arnarstapi / 🏠 The Governor's House That Left

en: Bárður again — and this time it's not a bath. Two boys, aged **eleven and twelve**. He took them **one under each arm**, walked up the mountain — and the gorge and the sea-crag where it ended **still carry their names**.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Arnarstapi → Ytri-Tunga / ⛰️ Stapafell & Rauðfeldsgjá

en: Iceland has, in its entire recorded history, essentially **one serial killer**. One. He farmed on **this coast** — and the travellers who crossed his path had a habit of **not continuing their journey**.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Arnarstapi → Ytri-Tunga / 🔪 Axlar-Björn

en: How does a small parish on a lava field get its church back? One widow. **Steinunn Sveinsdóttir** filed the paperwork with the church authorities, put up her own money, and **rebuilt it herself** — and the black church on that lava is hers.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Arnarstapi → Ytri-Tunga / ⛪ Búðir

en: The staff at this stop are unionised: they turn up in June and July, lie about all day, and get photographed doing it. **Seals. The staff are seals.**
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Ytri-Tunga / 🦭 Ytri-Tunga

en: The flat ground on your left used to be the **bottom of the sea** — and the cliffs on your *right* used to be the coastline. The land has been quietly standing up since the Ice Age ended. Iceland doesn't even hold still at the geography level.
ctx: opening hook line — tour 9.0 / Ytri-Tunga → Reykjavík / 🦅 Löngufjörur
